tables.name: ISO 8217 — Distillate Fuel Grades (Table 1)
rows: Emergency generators, lifeboat engines, very small high-speed diesels — not intended for main propulsion
Marine gas oil (MGO) — generators, ECA/port operation, low-sulphur trading, boiler pilot fuel
Similar to DMA with tighter cold-flow control; may include a permitted FAME (biodiesel) blend component
Marine diesel oil (MDO) — may contain trace residual content, used where DMA is unavailable

tables.name: ISO 8217 — Residual Fuel Grades (Table 2), by viscosity
rows: Widely used HFO grade for medium/low-speed main engines
Most common HFO grade historically bunkered for large 2-stroke main engines
Heaviest common grade, significant heating/handling requirements

tables.name: ISO 8217 — Key Fuel Quality Parameters Checked on a Bunker Test Report
rows: Used with corrected volume to calculate bunkered mass; typical ISO 8217 max ~991.0 kg/m3 for most residual grades (up to ~1010.0 kg/m3 for RMK grades), ~890.0 kg/m3 for distillates
Determines pumping and pre-injection heating requirements; too low or high versus the engine's design range risks injection pump/injector problems
Typical residual grade limit ~0.5% v/v; excess water risks injection equipment damage, incomplete combustion and microbial growth in storage
Regulated under MARPOL Annex VI — 0.50% m/m global cap, 0.10% m/m inside ECAs (or use of an approved equivalent such as a scrubber)
Indicates ignition quality of residual fuel; higher CCAI means poorer ignition quality/longer ignition delay — values above roughly 870 are considered a concern for many engines
SOLAS Chapter II-2 sets a 60°C minimum for fuel oils used on board — a hard safety limit, not just a quality parameter
Lowest temperature at which the fuel remains pumpable; sets minimum storage/transfer temperature
CCR / MCR (Conradson / Micro Carbon Residue) (% m/m)
Indicates coke-forming tendency in combustion, affecting deposits and ring/liner wear
Inorganic residue after combustion; contributes to abrasive wear and deposits
Trace metal from crude oil; contributes to high-temperature corrosion of exhaust valves and turbocharger components

Abrasive catalyst fines carried over from refinery processing; ISO 8217 sets a 60 mg/kg maximum as delivered — must be reduced further by onboard purification/settling before injection, as cat fines are a leading cause of severe cylinder liner and ring/piston wear
Indicates fuel stability and the risk of sludge formation, especially when blending fuels from different sources

tables.name: Marine Fuel Sulphur Categories (post-2020, MARPOL Annex VI)
rows: Only permitted with an approved equivalent means of compliance (typically an exhaust gas scrubber)
Default global-cap-compliant blend for use outside Emission Control Areas
Blend/residual-based product compliant for use inside Emission Control Areas without a scrubber
Distillate fuel meeting the ECA sulphur limit, also commonly used for boilers, generators and fuel changeover procedures

tables.name: Alternative & Future Marine Fuels — Overview
rows: Governed by the IGF Code; boil-off gas management, cryogenic burn hazard, gas detection and double-walled/inerted piping required
Toxic and burns with a nearly invisible flame; lower flash point than conventional fuel oil, needs dedicated fuel system and flame detection
Toxic (inhalation hazard) and corrosive to some materials; combustion produces no CO2 but requires careful NOx and unburnt-ammonia (slip) control
Wide flammability range and very low ignition energy; leak detection and ventilation are critical; storage volume is a major design constraint
Ambient temperature liquid, blended with conventional fuel
Can be used as drop-in blends in existing fuel systems within blend limits; more prone to microbial growth and oxidation in long-term storage than fossil fuel

tables.name: Lubricating Oil — ISO VG Viscosity Grade Series (Standard)
rows: Hydraulic systems, light machinery, some turbine oils
Medium-speed diesel engine crankcase (system oil), some compressors
Medium/low-speed diesel crankcase, cylinder oils (varies by BN), some gear oils

tables.name: Cylinder Oil — Base Number (BN) Selection Guide (general, follow engine maker's guidance)
rows: Very low sulphur fuel (< 0.10% S), e.g. ULSFO/MGO operation in ECAs
Low sulphur fuel (~0.50% S, VLSFO) — the common post-2020 default for most trading patterns
Legacy/traditional grade historically used for medium-sulphur HFO operation
Higher-sulphur HFO operation (e.g. with a scrubber, > 0.50% S) or per maker guidance for specific feed-rate strategies

tables.name: System (Crankcase) Oil — Trunk-Piston Engines, General Reference
Lubricating Oil — Key Terms
rows: Measure of an oil's reserve alkalinity (mg KOH/g), used to neutralise acidic combustion by-products formed from fuel sulphur — cylinder oil BN is selected to match the sulphur content of the fuel in use
Measure of how much an oil's viscosity changes with temperature — a higher VI means more stable viscosity across the engine's operating temperature range
Industry performance classifications (e.g. API CF/CF-4/CI-4 for diesel engine oils) referenced by engine makers alongside their own specific lubricant approval lists

tables.name: Common SI Units in the Engine Room
rows: Fuel typically ~980-991 kg/m3 @ 15°C for HFO; ~830-890 for MGO/MDO
Typical modern 2-stroke main engine: approx. 165-190 g/kWh

tables.name: Fuel Net Calorific Value (LHV) — Typical, Approximate
Fuel Density/Volume Correction (concept)
rows: Measured at ambient temperature by hydrometer or densitometer
Observed density corrected to a standard reference temperature (15°C) using ASTM/API/ISO correction tables (VCF - Volume Correction Factor), essential for accurate bunker quantity accounting
Bunker mass (metric tonnes) is calculated from corrected volume (m3) and density @15°C (kg/m3), not raw sounded volume alone
API = (141.5 / SG at 60°F) - 131.5; SG = 141.5 / (API + 131.5) — an alternate way fuel/lube quality certificates express density

tables.name: Electrical — Typical Shipboard Standards (general guidance, verify against class/flag rules and the ship's own drawings)
rows: High-voltage distribution (large ships, e.g. cruise/LNG/large container)

tables.name: Electrical — Quick Formulas
rows: P (W) = V x I x cos(phi)
P (W) = sqrt(3) x V(line) x I(line) x cos(phi)
S (VA) = sqrt(3) x V(line) x I(line)

tables.name: Insulation Resistance — General Guidance
rows: Often cited as 1 MΩ, or (rated voltage in kV + 1) MΩ, measured with a megger at the machine's rated DC test voltage
This is a general industry rule of thumb only — always follow the maker's manual, class society requirements and the ship's PMS/SMS acceptance criteria, which take precedence

tables.name: Engine Performance — Key Terms & Formulas
rows: Power developed inside the cylinder, derived from the indicator diagram (mean indicated pressure x length x area x speed, summed per cylinder)
Power actually delivered at the crankshaft/output flange, measured by a brake, dynamometer or torsion meter
Average effective cylinder pressure over one working cycle; IMEP from the indicator diagram, BMEP back-calculated from measured BHP
BHP / IHP — the fraction of indicated power that reaches the output shaft after friction losses
Fuel mass burned per unit of power per hour (g/kWh) — lower SFOC means better fuel efficiency
Useful work output / heat energy supplied by the fuel; large modern low-speed 2-stroke marine diesels typically reach roughly 50%

tables.name: Watchkeeping / PMS Checklist Themes (engine room)
rows: Cylinder exhaust temps, jacket cooling water temp/pressure, lube oil pressure/temp, turbocharger rpm/exhaust, crankcase oil mist detector status
Load sharing, cooling water/lube oil parameters, exhaust temps, running hours vs PMS due dates
Water level/gauge glass, steam pressure, water treatment (chemical dosing/TDS blowdown), safety valve test dates
Bowl condition, interface, sludge discharge, back-flush intervals
15 ppm alarm function test, valid calibration, bilge log entries matching Oil Record Book
Fixed fire-fighting system pressure/readiness, emergency fire pump, quick-closing valves/dampers free to operate
